subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class delegate-only per-agent tool policy, and if so should it be modeled as `tools.selfDeny`, a named delegation policy, or unified under the `toolsAllow` design?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but it changes a public config/security boundary and must preserve the deny-wins invariant without creating competing policy surfaces.

options.title: Define delegate-only policy now
options.body: Approve a narrow additive config/API contract for parent-self denial, require docs and tests for composition with inherited allow/deny and `toolsAllow`, and keep this issue open until implemented.

options.title: Fold into toolsAllow work
options.body: Make PR #78441 or its successor own both child narrowing and parent-self denial before this issue closes.

options.title: Reject core policy surface
options.body: Close this as out of core only if maintainers decide delegate-only permissions should live outside OpenClaw's runtime/config contract.

recommendation.title: Define delegate-only policy now
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow additive config/API contract for parent-self denial, require docs and tests for composition with inherited allow/deny and `toolsAllow`, and keep this issue open until implemented.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public tool-policy and security-boundary choice, and the available history points to steipete as the strongest adjacent owner-boundary reviewer.
